title: Layer-wise outlier mitigation and quant calibration for LLama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Background:
We are expanding Redwood's quantization profiles to cover FP8 and INT8 production variants for popular open models (LLaMA family, Mistral, Qwen). Early adopters report accuracy regressions that correlate to a small number of extreme per-layer outliers (weight and activation values) and to inconsistent layer-wise scaling choices made during one-shot calibration. This ticket scopes a pragmatic calibration/correction workflow and per-model heuristics to detect and mitigate outliers, produce stable per-layer scales, and validate accuracy across generation and downstream tasks.

Goals:
1) Define an automated calibration pipeline that produces repeatable per-layer scale factors for INT8/FP8 that are robust to outliers.
2) Implement model-specific outlier handlers (clipping, per-channel rescaling, hybrid fallback) for LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen families.
3) Add layer-wise scaling fixes to the quantizer that reduce accuracy regression to <=0.5% (relative) on our calibration and eval suites while preserving at least 10-15% throughput gains over FP16 baseline on target GPUs.
4) Integrate the validation suite into CI with regression alerts and produce a small playbook for live rollouts (canary criteria, rollback triggers).

Approach and design notes:
- Calibration dataset: use a 50k sample mix derived from the existing internal "calibration-corpus": 60% web text, 20% code, 20% instruction/QA pairs. Keep a held-out 5k set for validation metrics.
- Metrics: use KL-divergence of activation distributions (per-layer), 99.9th/99.99th percentile ranges, and downstream proxies: perplexity (LM), exact-match & F1 on a small QA/hallucination probe, and a short generation-quality scoring harness (nucleus sampling with token-level logprob regression).
- Outlier detection: compute per-layer activation weight histograms and track the 99.9/99.99 quantiles. Flag layers where the 99.99 quantile exceeds mean*X threshold (empirically X=35 for LLaMA, X=50 for Mistral gating layers, X=28 for Qwen embedding/heads).
- Mitigations: (a) asymmetric clipping at chosen percentile with retraining of scale; (b) per-channel max-abs rescaling for linear layers with large channel-wise variance; (c) per-layer hybrid mode: keep weight in INT8 but force FP16 activation computation for top-K offending layers; (d) small bias-correction step after quantization to zero-mean preserve.
- Layer-wise scaling fix: instead of global max-abs we propose a robust estimator: scale = max( max_abs, median_abs*alpha, percentile_99.9 ) with alpha set per-model (LLaMA=6, Mistral=8, Qwen=5). This avoids undue influence from single extreme outliers while still preserving dynamic range.
- Profiles: produce three profiles per-model: conservative (low perf risk), balanced (default), aggressive (max throughput, more likely to need hybrid fallbacks).

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Calibration harness updates: add percentile-based clipping knobs, per-channel rescaling option, and hybrid-layer override flags.
- Quantizer changes: implement robust scale estimator and support asymmetric clipping during weight/activation quantization. Add tests to ensure determinism given the same seed.
- Model-specific recipes: encode thresholds/alpha values for LLaMA-2 13B/70B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B/14B. Provide override map so we can tune live.
- Validation & CI: add end-to-end regression tests (perplexity + small downstream tasks) to be run on nightly hardware with representative quantized kernels (both CUDA and ROCm where available).

Notes on trade-offs and engineering constraints:
- PTQ approach prioritized (no QAT). QAT remains a follow-up for stubborn layers.
- Hybrid FP16 fallback increases memory & latency for those layers; we will prefer per-channel scaling first and only enable hybrid for layers that fail the accuracy threshold after clipping/scaling.
- FP8 path: FP8 dynamics differ (shared exponent behavior) — we need a dedicated kernel path. For now, our FP8 calibration will use the same outlier detection but introduce tighter percentile clipping (99.9) and a separate profile because FP8 is more sensitive to activation extremes.

Deliverables:
- New calibration harness and quantizer changes merged behind feature flag quant_layerwise_v2.
- Model-specific profile files committed to model-catalog (JSON).
- CI regression job and alerting rule (post-merge).
- Confluence playbook: rollout steps and manual remediation checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration pipeline produces reproducible per-layer scales (seeded) and the quantized model meets: <=0.5% relative perplexity regression vs FP16 on held-out set for balanced profile on each target model (LLaMA-2 13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-14B).
- For the conservative profile, regression <=0.2% and hybrid fallback used in no more than 3 layers per model.
- Throughput: balanced profile must show >=10% mean throughput improvement on test rig (A100x2) and aggressive >=22% improvement.
- CI runs must include at least 2 GPU variants and fail the release pipeline if regression >1.5%.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic calibration: repeated runs with same seed produce identical per-layer scale maps.
Balanced INT8 profile: <=0.5% relative perplexity regression vs FP16 on held-out LM calibration set for LLaMA-2 13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-14B.
Conservative profile: <=0.2% regression and <=3 hybrid-fallback layers per model.
Throughput: Balanced >=10% improvement on A100x2; Aggressive >=22% on same rig.
Nightly CI regression job added and alerts configured to notify runtime-ops on >1.0% regression.
Model profiles committed to model-catalog and documented in Confluence playbook.
PRs reviewed by at least one Runtime and one Applied-ML engineer and merged behind feature flag.
steps: Draft calibration algorithm and select default percentile thresholds (Aisha).
Instrument calibration harness to emit per-layer histograms and quantiles (Marco).
Run baseline PTQ on target models and collect failure-layer candidates (Marco + Lena).
Implement robust scale estimator and per-channel rescaling in quantizer (ENG PR).
Add hybrid-layer override and activation-FP16 fallback logic as runtime option.
Create model-specific recipe files and tune alpha/thresholds for each model.
Run end-to-end validation (perplexity + QA probes) and record metrics in results dashboard.
Open PR with changes, link to Confluence doc and results artifacts for review.
Merge behind feature flag, add CI jobs and nightly regressions, schedule rollout to canary tenants.
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Kapoor: Initial spike results show LLaMA-2 13B INT8 naive quantization had ~2.8% perplexity regression. Top 4 offending layers are attention Q/K projections and last MLP in each block.
2026-03-04 Marco Diaz: Implemented histogram exporter. Observed that Mistral gating layers have very heavy tails — 99.99 quantile 40x median. Suggest per-channel clipping + bias-correction.

2026-03-06 Lena Chen: Ran experiments with robust estimator (median_abs*alpha). Set alpha=8 for Mistral reduced regression to ~0.9% but still above target. Adding asymmetric clipping at 99.9th reduced to 0.45%.

2026-03-08 Marco Diaz: FP8 experiment: profile shows sensitivity to activation peaks; aggressive profile must clip earlier. Also flagged kernel work needed for shared-exponent FP8 path (opened ENG-4865).
2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created Confluence draft with playbook and sample commands for running calibration locally and in CI: https://confluence.internal/redwood/quant-calibration-playbook
2026-03-11 Code review: PR#219 has been opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quantization/pull/219). Runtime review requested from @lena-chen and @runtime-oncall.
notes: If some layers remain stubborn after PTQ interventions, schedule a follow-up ticket to explore lightweight QAT on affected layers only. Also coordinate with kernel team for FP8 native kernels (ENG-4865).
